questions.answer: Newton's Second Law of Motion states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass (F = ma).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with appropriate words.
questions.text: The electric charge generated by friction is called ______ electricity.
questions.answer: frictional

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: State whether the following statements are True or False.
questions.text: Repulsion is used as a test for identifying an electrically charged object.
questions.answer: True

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the scientists and devices with their relevant descriptions:
questions.answer: Benjamin Franklin - Named charges positive and negative; Thales - Found amber attracts feathers; Thomas Browne - Named the property 'electricity'; Gold leaf electroscope - Detects electric charge

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the Greek name for the yellow coloured amber?
questions.answer: Elektron

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why is frictional electricity called static electricity?
questions.answer: It is called static electricity because the charge is produced only at the place of friction and remains on the object for a short duration.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the given figure and answer the question.
questions.text: In the given figure, what interaction is shown in part A between the two glass rods and why?
questions.answer: Part A shows repulsion. This is because both glass rods carry similar charges, and two rods carrying similar charges push each other away.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the given figure and answer the question.
questions.text: In the given figure, what happens to the negative charges when the two substances are rubbed against each other?
questions.answer: When the objects are rubbed, the negative charges from one object go to the other object, making one positively charged and the other negatively charged.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Static electricity experiments should be performed in dry weather, particularly in winter.
questions.answer: This is because the charges of static electricity are absorbed in moist air; therefore, dry weather is necessary to observe the effects clearly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following question in brief.
questions.text: How does an atom become positively charged?
questions.answer: An atom is normally neutral. If for some reason the number of negative charges decreases or they go away, the atom becomes positively charged due to a deficiency of negative particles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Solve the following based on the principles of electric charge.
questions.text: An object has an equal number of positive and negative charges. If 500 negative particles are transferred from this object to another object by friction, what will be the nature of the net charge remaining on the first object?
questions.answer: The first object will become positively charged because it now has a deficiency of negatively charged particles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Describe the construction of a gold leaf electroscope.
questions.answer: It consists of a copper rod with a metal disc at the upper end and two thin gold leaves at the other end. The rod is placed in a bottle so the disc is above it. When a charged object touches the disc, the leaves gain the same charge and repel each other.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Use your brain power to answer.
questions.text: Why does a charged balloon stick to a wall?
questions.answer: When a charged balloon is brought near the wall, an opposite charge is generated on the wall by induction. Due to the attraction between these opposite charges, the balloon sticks to the wall.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Neutral object
questions.answer: When the positive charge (+) and negative charge (-) on an object are balanced, the object is said to be neutral.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What happens to the gold leaves of an electroscope when we touch the metal disc with our hand?
questions.answer: The leaves collapse because the charge in the leaves goes into the earth through our body, and the leaves get discharged.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the proper word from the brackets. (radiation, white, conduction, blue, convection, bad conductor, good conductor, black, reflection)
questions.text: Maximum heat is absorbed by a ______ colored object.
questions.answer: black

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the proper word from the brackets. (radiation, white, conduction, blue, convection, bad conductor, good conductor, black, reflection)
questions.text: ______ of heat does not require a medium.
questions.answer: Radiation

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the proper word from the brackets. (radiation, white, conduction, blue, convection, bad conductor, good conductor, black, reflection)
questions.text: Conduction of heat takes place through a ______ substance.
questions.answer: good conductor

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the proper word from the brackets. (radiation, white, conduction, blue, convection, bad conductor, good conductor, black, reflection)
questions.text: The shining surface in a thermos flask decreases the outgoing heat by ______.
questions.answer: reflection

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the proper word from the brackets. (radiation, white, conduction, blue, convection, bad conductor, good conductor, black, reflection)
questions.text: Cooking utensils are made from metals due to their property of ______.
questions.answer: conduction

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the proper word from the brackets. (radiation, white, conduction, blue, convection, bad conductor, good conductor, black, reflection)
questions.text: The earth receives heat from the sun by ______.
questions.answer: radiation

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What will absorb heat? Steel spoon, wooden board, glass vessel, iron griddle (tava), glass, wooden spoon, plastic plate, soil, water, wax
questions.answer: All the given objects will absorb heat to some extent, but steel spoon, iron griddle, soil, and water absorb it more effectively than wood or plastic.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: How does a fever get lowered by putting a cold compress on the forehead of a patient?
questions.answer: The water in the cold compress absorbs the heat from the patient's forehead and body, which helps in lowering the body temperature through conduction and evaporation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Why are the houses in Rajasthan painted white?
questions.answer: Rajasthan has a hot climate. White color reflects most of the radiant heat from the sun, keeping the inside of the houses cool.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What are the modes of heat transfer?
questions.answer: The three modes of heat transfer are conduction, convection, and radiation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Explain which mode of heat transfer causes sea breezes and land breezes.
questions.answer: Sea breezes and land breezes are caused by convection. During the day, land heats up faster than water, causing air above it to rise and cool air from the sea to blow in. At night, the process reverses.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Why is the outer coat of the penguins of Antarctica black?
questions.answer: The black color absorbs maximum heat from the sun, which helps the penguins to keep their bodies warm in the freezing temperatures of Antarctica.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Why are heaters fitted near the floor and air conditioners, near the ceiling of a room?
questions.answer: Hot air from heaters is lighter and rises up, creating convection currents that warm the room. Cold air from ACs is heavier and sinks down, cooling the room efficiently.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An ordinary glass bottle cracks when boiling water is poured into it, but a borosil glass bottle does not.
questions.answer: Ordinary glass is a poor conductor; the inner wall expands rapidly while the outer wall doesn't, causing it to crack. Borosil glass has a very low expansion coefficient and does not crack.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The telephone wires which sag in summer become straight in winter.
questions.answer: Metals expand on heating and contract on cooling. In summer, wires expand due to heat and sag; in winter, they contract and become straight.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Dew drops form on the grass, in winter.
questions.answer: In winter, the temperature of the air near the ground drops. The air becomes saturated with water vapor, which then condenses into water droplets on the cold grass.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In winter, why does an iron pillar feel colder than a wooden pole?
questions.answer: Iron is a good conductor of heat and quickly conducts heat away from our hand. Wood is a bad conductor and does not conduct heat away as fast, so it feels less cold.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Make a note of the various examples of heat transfer seen in day-to-day life.
questions.answer: Examples include heating a metal spoon in a cup of tea (conduction), boiling water in a kettle (convection), and feeling the heat of the sun (radiation).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Famine, earthquake, cloudburst, railway accident.
questions.answer: Railway accident. Reason: Famine, earthquake, and cloudburst are natural disasters, while a railway accident is a man-made disaster.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Drought, heavy rains, storm, tsunami.
questions.answer: Tsunami. Reason: Drought, heavy rains, and storms are atmospheric/weather-related disasters, whereas a tsunami is a geological disaster occurring in the ocean.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Lava, hot mud, ash, locusts.
questions.answer: Locusts. Reason: Lava, hot mud, and ash are products of a volcanic eruption, while locusts are a biological pest attack.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Washing away of crops, attack of pests on crops, volcano, singeing of crops.
questions.answer: Volcano. Reason: Others are specific factors that directly destroy crops, while a volcano is a geological disaster.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the remedial measures for the following calamities?
questions.text: Famine
questions.answer: Planned use of water and reuse of water, proper water management at local levels, and large-scale tree plantation to prevent erosion and maintain climate.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the remedial measures for the following calamities?
questions.text: Lightning strike
questions.answer: Stay indoors, do not stand under trees or on open ground, avoid using mobile phones or electrical appliances, and install lightning conductors on tall buildings.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the remedial measures for the following calamities?
questions.text: Storm
questions.answer: Move to a safe shelter, keep emergency contact numbers ready, inform others of the danger, and stay away from electric poles or weak structures.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the remedial measures for the following calamities?
questions.text: Cloudburst
questions.answer: Do not take shelter at the foot of a hill, move to higher ground immediately, and follow weather warnings issued by the meteorological department.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: True or false? Give reasons for your answer.
questions.text: Information about a forthcoming storm is to be kept secret.
questions.answer: False. Reason: Information about a storm should be widely publicized so that people can move to safe places and minimize the loss of life and property.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: True or false? Give reasons for your answer.
questions.text: You should not swim when there is lightning in the sky.
questions.answer: True. Reason: Water is a good conductor of electricity. If lightning strikes the water, it can cause a fatal electric shock to anyone swimming in it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: True or false? Give reasons for your answer.
questions.text: It is possible to prevent the eruption of a volcano.
questions.answer: False. Reason: A volcanic eruption is a natural geological process occurring due to movements deep inside the Earth's interior, which humans cannot control or prevent.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: True or false? Give reasons for your answer.
questions.text: Heavy rains result in famine.
questions.answer: True. Reason: Heavy rains lead to floods, which wash away crops and destroy agricultural land, leading to a shortage of food grains (famine).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: What is a tsunami? What gives rise to a tsunami?
questions.answer: A tsunami is a series of giant sea waves. It is caused by an earthquake or a volcanic eruption occurring on the ocean floor, which displaces a large volume of water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: What is a cloudburst?
questions.answer: A cloudburst is a sudden, very heavy rainfall in a small geographical area. It occurs when water vapor condenses rapidly, resulting in rainfall of 100 mm per hour or more.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Explain the effects of a volcano.
questions.answer: Volcanoes lead to the formation of new landforms like mountains. They release toxic gases and ash that pollute the environment. They can also cause forest fires and bury human settlements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: What are the measures to prevent loss of life due to lightning?
questions.answer: To prevent loss of life, install lightning conductors on buildings. During a storm, avoid standing near tall objects, trees, or water bodies. Stay indoors and avoid using plugged-in electronic devices.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What measures have been taken to deal with calamities such as floods and landslides under the disaster management programme in Maharashtra?
questions.answer: Maharashtra has established a Disaster Management Cell. Measures include satellite-based weather monitoring, construction of protective walls in landslide-prone areas, and training rescue teams like the NDRF.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: With reference to disaster management what are the things in your house that you will check?
questions.answer: I will check for cracks in the walls, ensure the first aid kit is fully stocked, check if heavy cupboards are secured to walls, and verify that emergency torches and batteries are working.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is a ‘cell’?
questions.answer: The cell is the fundamental, structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Name the different organelles in a cell?
questions.answer: The different organelles in a cell include the nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi body, lysosomes, mitochondria, vacuoles, and plastids.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are micro-organisms?
questions.answer: Organisms which cannot be seen with our eyes but only under a microscope are called micro-organisms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which are the different types of micro-organisms?
questions.answer: Micro-organisms are classified into bacteria, viruses, algae, fungi, and protozoa.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the proper word.
questions.text: The organelle called the ______ is present in plant cells only.
questions.answer: chloroplast

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the proper word.
questions.text: Garbage is converted into ______ by micro-organisms.
questions.answer: manure

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the proper word.
questions.text: In the cell, photosynthesis is carried out with the help of ______.
questions.answer: chloroplasts

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the proper word.
questions.text: An electron microscope is necessary for the study of ______.
questions.answer: micro-organisms

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plant cell and animal cell.
questions.answer: Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts, whereas animal cells lack them. Plant cells have a large central vacuole, while animal cells have small vacuoles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Prokaryotic cell and eukaryotic cell.
questions.answer: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles, whereas eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Sketch and describe in your own words, the plant cell and animal cell.
questions.text: Sketch and describe in your own words, the plant cell and animal cell.
questions.answer: Students should draw labeled diagrams of both cells and describe components like the cell wall (in plants), nucleus, and mitochondria.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain the uses and the harmful effects of micro-organisms.
questions.answer: Uses: Fermentation, nitrogen fixation, and waste decomposition. Harmful effects: Causing diseases like cholera and spoiling food.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Diseases spread on a large scale during periods of heavy rainfall and floods.
questions.answer: Floodwaters contaminate drinking water sources with sewage and pathogens, leading to the rapid spread of infectious diseases.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: There is a possibility of food poisoning if we eat stale food.
questions.answer: Stale food allows micro-organisms to grow and produce toxic substances that cause illness when consumed.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Soil is turned over during tilling.
questions.answer: Tilling aerates the soil and mixes organic matter, which promotes the activity of beneficial microbes that increase fertility.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Fungus grows quickly in moist or humid conditions.
questions.answer: Moisture and warmth provide the necessary environment for fungal spores to germinate and multiply rapidly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A refrigerator is used in almost every home.
questions.answer: The low temperature in a refrigerator inhibits the growth of micro-organisms, keeping food fresh for a longer time.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Bread ‘rises’ during baking.
questions.answer: Yeast ferments sugar in the dough, releasing carbon dioxide gas which expands and makes the bread porous and light.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Fodder is soaked in water before offering to cattle.
questions.answer: Soaking softens the fodder and allows microbes to begin breaking down complex fibers, making it easier for cattle to digest.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: When will you use a simple microscope and when, a compound microscope? Explain in detail how you will use them.
questions.answer: A simple microscope is used for low magnification of larger objects. A compound microscope is used for high magnification of cells. They are used by placing the specimen on a slide and adjusting the focus.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Visit a bakery in your area, collect information about the process of manufacture of their products and make one of them at home.
questions.answer: Students should document the use of yeast in fermentation during their bakery visit and attempt a simple baking recipe at home.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: The process of digestion starts from the ______ (stomach / mouth).
questions.answer: mouth

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Eyelids have ______ muscles that perform an involuntary role (voluntary / involuntary).
questions.answer: involuntary

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Muscles of the heart are ______ muscles (ordinary muscles / cardiac muscles).
questions.answer: cardiac

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Pushing forward the food that has been chewed is the function of the ______ (stomach / oesophagus).
questions.answer: oesophagus

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: The cardiac muscles do not move.
questions.answer: The heart keeps beating continuously; if cardiac muscles stopped moving, the heart would cease to pump blood, leading to loss of circulation and death.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Food enters the stomach and ______ the stomach muscles do not move.
questions.answer: if the stomach muscles do not contract, food would not be churned and digestion would be severely impaired.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Cardiac muscles always function. Which are those types?
questions.answer: Cardiac, skeletal, and smooth muscles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: What causes the problem of acidity?
questions.answer: Excess stomach acid or reflux of acid into the esophagus.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: What is its effect on the body?
questions.answer: Acidity can damage the lining of the stomach and esophagus, causing pain and ulcers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: We never feel about by muscles ______ tired.
questions.answer: when muscles are tired, we feel fatigue and reduced strength.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Pepsin
questions.answer: Pepsin is a digestive enzyme that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides in the stomach.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Cramps

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Skeletal muscles
questions.answer: Skeletal muscles are voluntary muscles attached to bones.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Who is telling a lie?
questions.answer: The statement that only a sweet taste can be detected by the tongue is false; the tongue can detect sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and umami.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Muscular System and Digestive System in Human Beings
questions.text: Liver
questions.answer: The liver is the largest gland in the body and processes nutrients, detoxifies blood, and stores bile.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the right word from the brackets.
questions.text: The process of digestion starts from the ______.
questions.answer: mouth

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the right word from the brackets.
questions.text: Eyelids have ______ muscles.
questions.answer: involuntary

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the right word from the brackets.
questions.text: ______ is not a function of the muscular system.
questions.answer: Production of blood cells

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the right word from the brackets.
questions.text: Muscles of the heart are ______.
questions.answer: cardiac muscles

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the right word from the brackets.
questions.text: Pushing forward the food that has been chewed is the function of the ______.
questions.answer: oesophagus

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the items in Group 'A' with their correct descriptions in Group 'B'.
pairs: uncontrolled and painful contraction of muscles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Organ: Tongue. Statement: My taste-buds can tell only a sweet taste.
questions.answer: The Tongue is lying. Taste buds can detect sweet, sour, salty, and bitter tastes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Organ: Liver. Statement: I am the largest gland in the body.
questions.answer: The Liver is telling the truth. It is indeed the largest gland in the human body.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Organ: Large intestine. Statement: I am 7.5 meter long.
questions.answer: The Large intestine is lying. It is about 1.5 meters long, while the small intestine is 7.5 meters long.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Organ: Appendix. Statement: Digestion is impossible without me.
questions.answer: The Appendix is lying. It is a vestigial organ and does not perform any function in human digestion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Organ: Lung. Statement: I play an important role in excretion.
questions.answer: The Lung is telling the truth. It excretes carbon dioxide and water vapor from the body.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Food becomes acidic in the stomach.
questions.answer: Food becomes acidic because the gastric juice in the stomach contains hydrochloric acid (HCl), which helps in digestion and killing bacteria.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Cardiac muscles are said to be involuntary muscles.
questions.answer: Cardiac muscles are involuntary because their movements (contraction and relaxation) are not under the control of our will; they function automatically throughout life.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Intoxicating substances should not be consumed.
questions.answer: Intoxicating substances like tobacco or alcohol damage the liver, digestive system, and nervous system, leading to serious health issues like cancer.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Your muscles should be strong and efficient.
questions.answer: Muscles must be strong to perform various physical activities, maintain correct body posture, and ensure the proper functioning of internal organs.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How many types of muscles are there? Which are those types?
questions.answer: There are three types of muscles: 1. Skeletal (Voluntary) muscles, 2. Cardiac muscles, and 3. Smooth (Involuntary) muscles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What causes the problem of acidity? What is its effect on the body?
questions.answer: Acidity is caused by excessive secretion of HCl, often due to spicy food or irregular eating habits. It causes a burning sensation in the chest and stomach.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Name the different types of teeth. What is the function of each type?
questions.answer: 1. Incisors (cutting), 2. Canines (tearing), 3. Premolars (chewing/grinding), 4. Molars (chewing/grinding).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Sketch and label a diagram of the digestive system and describe it in your own words.
questions.text: Sketch and label a diagram of the digestive system and describe it in your own words.
questions.answer: Student should draw a diagram showing mouth, oesophagus, stomach, liver, pancreas, small and large intestines. Description should mention the path of food and role of enzymes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Physical change and chemical change
questions.answer: Physical change is temporary and reversible where no new substance is formed (e.g., melting ice). Chemical change is permanent and irreversible where a new substance is formed (e.g., burning wood).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Periodic change and non-periodic change
questions.answer: Periodic changes occur at regular intervals of time (e.g., day and night). Non-periodic changes do not occur at fixed intervals (e.g., earthquake).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Natural change and man-made change
questions.answer: Natural changes occur on their own in nature (e.g., ripening of fruit). Man-made changes are brought about by human activities (e.g., making furniture from wood).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Under which different types can the following change be classified?
questions.text: Conversion of milk into yoghurt.
questions.answer: Chemical change, Irreversible change, Man-made change.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Under which different types can the following change be classified?
questions.text: Bursting of a cracker.
questions.answer: Chemical change, Fast change, Irreversible change.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Under which different types can the following change be classified?
questions.text: Occurrence of an earthquake.
questions.answer: Natural change, Non-periodic change, Fast change.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Under which different types can the following change be classified?
questions.text: Revolution of an earth around the sun.
questions.answer: Natural change, Periodic change, Slow change.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Under which different types can the following change be classified?
questions.text: Stretching of a spring.
questions.answer: Physical change, Reversible change.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: While purchasing canned food, its expiry date should be checked.
questions.answer: Canned food undergoes chemical changes over time which may produce toxins or spoil the food, making it unsafe for consumption after the expiry date.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An iron article should be given a coat of paint.
questions.answer: Painting prevents iron from coming into contact with moisture and oxygen in the air, thereby preventing the chemical change of rusting.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A wooden article should be polished.
questions.answer: Polishing creates a protective layer that prevents the wood from decaying due to moisture or insect attacks, maintaining its quality.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Copper and brass utensils should be tinned.
questions.answer: Tinning prevents the reaction between the metal and acidic substances in food, which could otherwise lead to food poisoning (corrosion).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A dry handkerchief gets wet at once on dipping in water, but it takes long for a wet handkerchief to dry.
questions.answer: Wetting is a fast process of absorption, whereas drying involves evaporation, which is a slow process dependent on temperature and humidity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the items in Group 'A' with their correct description in Group 'B'.
questions.answer: Stainless steel - Alloy, Silver - Metal, Bhajani mixture for milling - Mixture, Salt - Compound, Coal - Non-metal, Hydrogen - Element

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the names of elements to the following symbols.
questions.text: Zn, Cd, Xe, Br, Ti, Cu, Fe, Si, Ir, Pt
questions.answer: Zn: Zinc, Cd: Cadmium, Xe: Xenon, Br: Bromine, Ti: Titanium, Cu: Copper, Fe: Iron, Si: Silicon, Ir: Iridium, Pt: Platinum

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the molecular formulae of the following compounds?
questions.text: Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, sodium chloride, glucose, methane.
questions.answer: Hydrochloric acid: HCl, Sulphuric acid: H2SO4, Sodium chloride: NaCl, Glucose: C6H12O6, Methane: CH4

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Buttermilk is churned to get butter.
questions.answer: Butter particles are lighter than the rest of the buttermilk. Churning is a form of centrifugation where the lighter butter particles separate and collect together, making them easy to remove.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In chromatography, the ingredients of a mixture rise up to a limited height when water rises up to the upper end of the paper.
questions.answer: The ingredients rise based on two factors: their solubility in the rising solvent and their ability to stick to the filter paper. Since these properties differ for each ingredient, they stop at different heights.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A wet cloth is wrapped around a water storage container in summer.
questions.answer: The water in the wet cloth evaporates by absorbing heat from the container and the water inside it. This loss of heat results in the cooling of the water stored in the container.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Metals and non-metals
questions.answer: Metals have luster, are malleable, ductile, and are good conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals generally lack luster, are brittle in solid state, and are poor conductors of heat and electricity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Mixtures and compounds
questions.answer: Compounds are formed by chemical combination of elements in fixed proportions and have different properties than their constituents. Mixtures are formed by physical mixing in any proportion and constituents retain their properties.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Atoms and molecules
questions.answer: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that cannot be further divided by chemical means. A molecule is formed by the chemical combination of two or more atoms of the same or different elements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Separation by distillation and by separating funnel
questions.answer: Distillation is used to separate miscible liquids with different boiling points or a soluble solid from a liquid. A separating funnel is used to separate two immiscible liquids based on their different densities.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: How are the components of mixtures separated by simple methods?
questions.answer: Components of mixtures can be separated by simple physical methods such as straining, filtering, sifting, picking, sorting, winnowing, using a magnet, and sublimation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Which elements (metals and non-metals), compounds and mixtures do we use in our day-to-day life?
questions.answer: Elements: Iron (metal), Oxygen (non-metal). Compounds: Common salt (NaCl), Water (H2O), Sugar. Mixtures: Air, Milk, Brass utensils, and food items like Bhel.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: In everyday life, where and for what purpose do we use centrifugation?
questions.answer: Centrifugation is used in dairies to separate cream from milk, in laboratories to separate blood cells from plasma, and in washing machines to remove water from wet clothes by spinning.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Where are the methods of separation by distillation and by separating funnel used? Why?
questions.answer: Distillation is used in labs to get pure water and in industries to separate components of crude oil because they have different boiling points. Separating funnels are used to separate oil and water because they do not mix and have different densities.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Which precaution will you take while using the methods of distillation and separation by separating funnel?
questions.answer: Precautions include ensuring the apparatus is airtight, handling the burner carefully, ensuring the condenser has a constant water supply, and carefully opening the stopcock of the separating funnel to avoid mixing layers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Visit a jaggery or a sugar factory. Obtain information about the methods that are used to separate the components of the mixture while making jaggery or sugar. Present it in the class.
questions.answer: Students should observe processes like filtration of sugarcane juice to remove impurities, evaporation of water by heating the juice, and crystallization to obtain sugar crystals from the concentrated syrup.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill appropriate terms in the blanks.
questions.text: The substance that helps water to remove dirt from the surface of materials is called ______.
questions.answer: detergent

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill appropriate terms in the blanks.
questions.text: Fluoride is used in toothpaste to prevent ______.
questions.answer: tooth decay

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill appropriate terms in the blanks.
questions.text: Soap is a salt of ______ and sodium hydroxide.
questions.answer: fatty acid

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill appropriate terms in the blanks.
questions.text: Synthetic detergents can be used in ______ water as well.
questions.answer: hard

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill appropriate terms in the blanks.
questions.text: For construction purposes ______ cement is the most commonly used cement.
questions.answer: Portland

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: How does the use of a detergent help to clean soiled clothes?
questions.answer: A molecule of a detergent holds on to a water molecule at one end and an oil molecule at the other. This allows the oil to mix with water, and the dirt on the clothes is removed with the water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: How will you check with the help of soap powder whether water is hard?
questions.answer: Add soap powder to the water and stir. If the water does not form a lather but instead forms a white scum (precipitate), then the water is hard.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What are the important ingredients of a toothpaste, and what is the function of each?
questions.answer: Calcium carbonate and dicalcium phosphate remove dirt and polish teeth. Fluoride prevents tooth decay by strengthening enamel. Flavours and humectants provide taste and keep the paste moist.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What are the ingredients of cement?
questions.answer: Cement is made from silica (sand), alumina (aluminium oxide), lime (calcium oxide), iron oxide, and magnesia (magnesium oxide).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What will happen if cement is not used in making concrete?
questions.answer: If cement is not used, the mixture of stones, sand, and water will not bind together. The resulting structure will lack strength, stability, and durability, eventually collapsing.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Make a list of detergents that you use.
questions.answer: Common detergents used include soap nuts (ritha), soap pods (shikekai), bathing soap, washing powder, liquid soap, and shampoo.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What should be expected from a detergent for delicate garments?
questions.answer: A detergent for delicate garments should be mild, pH neutral, easily soluble, and should not contain harsh chemicals that damage natural fibers like silk or wool.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What is meant by ‘surface activity’? Name three chemicals responsible for the surface activity of various detergents.
questions.answer: Surface activity is the property of a substance to spread easily on a surface and reduce the surface tension of a liquid. Chemicals responsible include sodium lauryl sulphate, sodium dodecyl benzene sulphonate, and various fatty acid salts.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the similarities and differences between -
questions.text: Natural detergents and man-made detergents
questions.answer: Similarity: Both are used for cleaning and removing dirt. Difference: Natural detergents (like ritha) contain saponin and are eco-friendly; man-made detergents are synthetic chemicals and may cause skin irritation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the similarities and differences between -
questions.text: Soap and synthetic detergent
questions.answer: Similarity: Both lower surface tension and remove oil/dirt. Difference: Soap is made from natural fats and does not work in hard water; synthetic detergents are made from petroleum/chemicals and work in hard water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the similarities and differences between -
questions.text: Bath soap and soap for washing clothes
questions.answer: Similarity: Both are salts of fatty acids. Difference: Bath soap uses potassium salts and is gentle on skin; washing soap uses sodium salts and is harsher to effectively remove tough stains from fabric.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What are the similarities and differences between -
questions.text: Modern cement and ancient cement
questions.answer: Similarity: Both are used as binding materials in construction. Difference: Ancient cement was made from volcanic ash and lime (Roman) or mixtures of oil and lime; modern Portland cement is a complex mixture of silica, alumina, and lime.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Soap cannot be used in hard water.
questions.answer: In hard water, soap reacts with calcium and magnesium salts to form an insoluble white scum (precipitate). This prevents the soap from forming a lather and cleaning effectively.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Oil does not mix in water. However, oil and water become homogeneous if a sufficient quantity of detergent is added.
questions.answer: Detergent molecules are long; one end holds a water molecule and the other holds an oil molecule. This allows oil to be suspended in water, forming a homogeneous mixture.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Synthetic detergents are superior to soap.
questions.answer: Synthetic detergents are superior because they can be used in hard water without forming scum, they are more effective at removing grease, and their properties can be tailored for specific uses.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Often coloured spots are formed on clothes during washing.
questions.answer: Coloured spots (like yellow turmeric stains turning red) occur because soaps and detergents are alkaline in nature and react chemically with certain natural pigments in the stains.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Tobacco masheri should not be used for cleaning teeth.
questions.answer: Masheri contains tobacco which is carcinogenic and causes oral cancer. It also stains the teeth and damages the gums and enamel.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Visit a cement factory. See how cement is prepared and discuss the process.
questions.answer: Student should observe the raw materials (limestone, clay), the heating in the kiln, and the grinding process to form cement powder.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write a conversation based on cement houses, mud-houses and wattle-and-daub houses.
questions.answer: The conversation should compare the durability and strength of cement houses with the eco-friendliness and temperature regulation of mud and wattle-and-daub houses.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Describe natural resources with reference to the following type.
questions.text: Mineral resources
questions.answer: Mineral resources are substances formed by natural processes in the earth's crust. They include metals like iron, gold, and copper, as well as non-metals like mica and sulfur. They are essential for industrial growth and are obtained through mining.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Describe natural resources with reference to the following type.
questions.text: Forest resources
questions.answer: Forests are an extensive area of land covered by a variety of plants. They provide wood, medicinal plants, rubber, and honey. They also help in maintaining the balance of atmospheric gases and preventing soil erosion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Describe natural resources with reference to the following type.
questions.text: Ocean resources
questions.answer: Oceans provide a vast variety of resources including biotic resources like fish, shells, and pearls, and mineral resources like thorium, magnesium, and common salt. They are also a source of energy through waves and tides.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: What is meant by fossil fuel? What are their types?
questions.answer: Fossil fuels are energy-rich substances formed from the remains of plants and animals buried underground millions of years ago. The main types are coal, mineral oil (petroleum), and natural gas.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: Make a list of the components we obtain from mineral oil.
questions.answer: The components obtained from mineral oil through fractional distillation include petrol, diesel, kerosene, naphtha, lubricating oil, paraffin wax, and tar.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: What do we get from forests?
questions.answer: We get wood for construction and fuel, medicinal plants (like Adulsa, Ashwagandha), fruits, gum, resin, honey, and raw materials for industries like paper and rubber.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: What are the items included in ocean resources? What are their uses?
questions.answer: Ocean resources include fish (food), pearls and shells (ornaments), salt (food/industry), and minerals like magnesium and potassium. They are used for nutrition, medicine, and industrial production.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: Why should we prevent the wastage of fuel used for vehicles?
questions.answer: Fossil fuels are non-renewable and take millions of years to form. Their supply is limited, and excessive use leads to air pollution and global warming. Saving fuel ensures it lasts longer for future generations.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: Why is the diversity of plants and animals in the forests declining?
questions.answer: Diversity is declining due to deforestation for agriculture and housing, illegal hunting, forest fires, and pollution. Loss of habitat makes it difficult for various species to survive and reproduce.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: Write the names of five minerals and the useful substances obtained from them.
questions.answer: 1. Iron ore (Iron), 2. Bauxite (Aluminium), 3. Cuprite (Copper), 4. Manganese ore (Manganese), 5. Mica (Insulating materials).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answer to the following question in your own words.
questions.text: Name the two important stages in the process of obtaining metals from ores?
questions.answer: The two important stages are extraction and purification of the metal.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What steps are taken for protection and conservation of natural resources?
questions.answer: Steps include: 1. Reducing wastage and recycling materials. 2. Using alternative renewable energy sources like solar and wind. 3. Afforestation. 4. Strict laws against illegal mining and hunting.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: In the given figure, complete the flow chart of fuels.
questions.text: Identify the missing categories and examples in the provided flow chart for Fossil Fuels.
questions.answer: The missing boxes are: 1. Coal (under Solid), 2. Liquid (above Mineral oil), 3. Gas (above Natural gas). Examples for Liquid: Petrol/Diesel; Examples for Gas: Methane/Ethane.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How can the economic condition of a nation depend on its natural resources?
questions.answer: A nation's economy depends on resources for industrial production, energy, and export. Abundant resources reduce import costs and create jobs, while their depletion can lead to economic instability and dependence on other countries.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which medicinal plants will you grow on your school premises and near your house? Why?
questions.answer: I would grow Tulsi and Adulsa for treating coughs and colds, and Aloe Vera for skin health. These plants are easy to maintain and provide immediate natural remedies for common ailments.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: When the beams from the headlights of a car fall on an object in the night, the shadows called ______ and ______ can be seen.
questions.answer: umbra, penumbra

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: During a lunar eclipse the shadow of the ______ falls on the ______.
questions.answer: Earth, Moon

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: During a solar eclipse the shadow of the ______ falls on the ______.
questions.answer: Moon, Earth

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Various shades of colour are seen in the sky at sunrise and sunset due to ______.
questions.answer: scattering of light

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Space beyond the earth's atmosphere appears dark.
questions.answer: In space, there is no atmosphere and hence no particles to scatter sunlight. Since there is no scattering of light, the space appears dark.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: We are able to read while sitting in the shade.
questions.answer: We can read in the shade because of the indirect light that reaches us after being scattered by the particles in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: We should not observe the solar eclipse with naked eyes.
questions.answer: During a solar eclipse, ultra-violet rays which are harmful to the eyes reach the earth. Observing it with naked eyes can cause permanent damage to the retina.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give one example of scattering of light that we come across in day-to-day life.
questions.text: Give one example of scattering of light that we come across in day-to-day life.
questions.answer: The blue color of the sky during the day is a common example of scattering of light.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why is the shadow of a bird flying high not seen on the earth?
questions.answer: When a bird flies at a high altitude, the umbra (dark shadow) does not reach the ground, and the penumbra is so faint and spread out that it is not visible.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why is a penumbra not obtained from a point source?
questions.answer: A point source of light has no dimensions. Light rays originate from a single point, so they either hit the object or pass it, creating only a sharp dark shadow (umbra) without any partial shadow (penumbra).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: What is meant by scattering of light?
questions.answer: Scattering of light is the process where light rays are redirected in various directions when they strike atoms, molecules, or tiny particles in the medium.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Does the shadow really vanish in the zero shadow condition?
questions.answer: No, the shadow does not vanish. In the zero shadow condition, the sun is exactly overhead, so the shadow falls exactly below the object and is not visible.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Will the laser beam be seen if it passes through a glass box which contains a lighted incense stick?
questions.answer: Yes, the laser beam will be seen because the smoke particles from the incense stick will scatter the laser light, making the path of the beam visible.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write a science based paragraph on 'What if the sun did not rise?'
questions.answer: If the sun did not rise, the earth would be plunged into permanent darkness and extreme cold. Photosynthesis would stop, leading to the death of plants and eventually all living organisms, ending life on Earth.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What efforts will you make to remove the misconceptions about eclipses?
questions.answer: I will organize awareness programs, explain the scientific geometry of eclipses using models, and encourage people to watch eclipses safely to prove they are natural phenomena and not bad omens.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Various eclipses and the conditions during that period.
questions.answer: Solar Eclipse: Occurs on a new moon day when the Moon is between the Sun and Earth. Lunar Eclipse: Occurs on a full moon night when the Earth is between the Sun and Moon.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Point sources and extended sources of light.
questions.answer: A point source is a tiny source of light that creates only an umbra. An extended source has a definite size and creates both an umbra and a penumbra.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Umbra and penumbra.
questions.answer: Umbra is the darkest, central part of a shadow where no light reaches. Penumbra is the partial, lighter shadow surrounding the umbra where only some light reaches.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Obtain information about the special goggles used to watch a solar eclipse.
questions.answer: Special solar filters or eclipse glasses are made of black polymer or aluminized Mylar that block 99.9% of sunlight and harmful UV/IR radiation to protect the eyes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Sound is generated by the rhythmic ______ of any object.
questions.answer: vibration

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The frequency of sound is measured in ______.
questions.answer: Hertz (Hz)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If ______ of sound is decreased, its loudness also decreases.
questions.answer: amplitude

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A medium is necessary for ______ of sound.
questions.answer: propagation

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the items in Group 'A' with Group 'B'.
questions.answer: Flute-Vibrations in the air, Frequency-Measured in Hz, Sound level-Decibel, Ultrasonic sound-Frequency more than 20000 Hz, Infrasonic sound-Frequency less than 20 Hz

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In earlier times, people used to listen for the arrival of a distant train by putting their ear to the rail.
questions.answer: Sound travels faster and more efficiently through solids (the steel rail) than through the air. By putting their ear to the rail, people could hear the vibrations of a distant train long before the sound reached them through the air.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The sounds generated by a tabla and a sitar are different.
questions.answer: The sounds are different because they are produced by different vibrating bodies; a tabla uses a vibrating stretched membrane, while a sitar uses vibrating stretched strings. This results in different frequencies and sound qualities.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If you were both on the moon, your friend will not be able to hear you call.
questions.answer: Sound requires a material medium like air, water, or solids to travel. Since the moon has no atmosphere (it is a vacuum), sound waves cannot propagate, making it impossible to hear a call.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: We can hear the movement of a mosquito’s wings but we cannot hear the movement of our hands.
questions.answer: Mosquito wings vibrate at a very high frequency that falls within the human audible range (20 Hz to 20,000 Hz). The movement of our hands produces vibrations at a very low frequency (infrasonic), which the human ear cannot detect.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: How is sound produced?
questions.answer: Sound is produced by the vibrations of an object. When an object vibrates, it causes the particles in the surrounding medium to vibrate, which eventually reaches our ears as sound.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: What does the intensity of sound depend upon?
questions.answer: The intensity of sound depends on the amplitude of the vibration (intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude) and the distance of the listener from the source of the sound.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Explain how the frequency of oscillation is related to the length of a pendulum and the amplitude of its oscillation.
questions.answer: The frequency of oscillation decreases as the length of the pendulum increases. However, the frequency remains constant regardless of the amplitude of the oscillation, provided the length stays the same.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions.
questions.text: Explain the two ways by which the pitch of the sound generated by a stretched string can be changed.
questions.answer: The pitch can be changed by: 1. Altering the tension of the string (increasing tension increases pitch). 2. Altering the vibrating length of the string (decreasing the length increases the pitch).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The bat, a mammal, flies during the night manoeuvering with the help of the ultrasonic sounds it produces. Find out more about this.
questions.answer: Bats use a process called echolocation. They emit high-frequency ultrasonic sounds that bounce off objects in their path. By sensing the returning echoes, they can determine the distance, size, and location of obstacles or insects.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the appropriate term in the blanks.
questions.text: The alloys called ______ and ______ are used for making industrial magnets.
questions.answer: alnico, nipermag

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the appropriate term in the blanks.
questions.text: A magnetic field can pass through ______ and ______.
questions.answer: cardboard, water

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the appropriate term in the blanks.
questions.text: The intensity of a magnetic field is indicated by the lines of ______.
questions.answer: force

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the appropriate term in the blanks.
questions.text: The real test of a magnet is ______.
questions.answer: repulsion

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: With whom should I pair up?
questions.text: Match Group A with Group B.
questions.answer: Compass-A magnetic needle, Door of a cupboard-A magnet, Repulsion-Like poles, Magnetic pole-The highest magnetic force

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions:
questions.text: Distinguish between the two methods of making artificial magnets.
questions.answer: In the Single Touch method, a steel bar is rubbed by one pole of a magnet in one direction, creating low-power temporary magnetism. In the Double Touch method, two opposite poles of two magnets are rubbed from the center to opposite ends, creating longer-lasting and stronger magnetism.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions:
questions.text: Which substances are used for making electromagnets?
questions.answer: An iron nail (or soft iron core), insulated copper wire, and a source of electric current like a battery are used for making electromagnets.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions:
questions.text: Write a note on 'magnetic field'.
questions.answer: The region around a magnet where the magnetic force acts on an object is called a magnetic field. It is represented by magnetic lines of force. The intensity is higher where lines are crowded and lower where they are sparse.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions:
questions.text: Why is a magnetic needle used in a compass?
questions.answer: A magnetic needle is a small magnet that is free to rotate. Due to the Earth's magnetic field, it always aligns itself in the North-South direction, which helps travelers determine directions accurately.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write answers to the following questions:
questions.text: Explain with the help of a diagram how the intensity of and direction of the magnetic field of a bar magnet can be determined.
questions.answer: Place a bar magnet on paper and sprinkle iron filings or use a magnetic compass. The filings align along lines of force showing direction (North to South). The density of filings near the poles indicates high intensity, while fewer filings in the middle indicate low intensity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give detailed information about the following:
questions.text: Give detailed information about how the merchants of olden times used a magnet while travelling.
questions.answer: Olden merchants used a naturally occurring magnetic rock called 'lodestone'. When suspended freely, it always pointed in the North-South direction. By observing this, they could navigate the seas and unknown lands even when the sun or stars were not visible.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Obtain information about the function of metal detectors.
questions.answer: Metal detectors work on the principle of electromagnetism. They contain a coil of wire that produces a magnetic field. When a metal object passes through this field, it induces an electric current in the object, which the detector senses and alerts the user.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the proper words in the blanks. (meridian, horizon, twelve, nine, apparent, celestial, ecliptic)
questions.text: When seen from a great distance, the sky seems to be touching the ground along a circle. This circle is called the ______.
questions.answer: horizon

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the proper words in the blanks. (meridian, horizon, twelve, nine, apparent, celestial, ecliptic)
questions.text: The ______ is used while defining the zodiac signs.
questions.answer: ecliptic

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the proper words in the blanks. (meridian, horizon, twelve, nine, apparent, celestial, ecliptic)
questions.text: Classified according to seasons, one season will have ______ nakshatras.
questions.answer: nine

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Write the proper words in the blanks. (meridian, horizon, twelve, nine, apparent, celestial, ecliptic)
questions.text: The rising of the sun in the east and its setting in the west is the ______ motion of the sun.
questions.answer: apparent

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A star rises at 8 pm tonight. At what time will it rise after a month? Why?
questions.answer: The star will rise at 6 pm. This is because stars rise 4 minutes earlier every day. In 30 days, the time difference becomes 120 minutes (30 x 4 = 120), which is equal to 2 hours.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is meant by ‘The sun enters a nakshatra’? It is said that in the rainy season, the sun enters the Mrug nakshatra. What does it mean?
questions.answer: When we look at the Sun from Earth, it appears to be in front of a particular nakshatra on the ecliptic. This is called 'entering a nakshatra'. Sun entering Mrug nakshatra means that from Earth, the Sun and Mrug constellation are in the same line of sight.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is a constellation?
questions.answer: A group of stars occupying a small portion of the celestial sphere is called a constellation. Some of these stars often appear to form the figure of some animal, object or person.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What points should be considered before a sky watch?
questions.answer: 1. The place for sky watching should be away from city lights and should be dark. 2. A new moon night is best. 3. Binoculars or a telescope should be used. 4. A star map and a torch with red cloth should be carried.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Is it wrong to say that the planets, stars and nakshatras affect human life? Why?
questions.answer: Yes, it is wrong. Science has proved that the position of celestial bodies has no influence on human destiny or personality. It is a superstition and not based on any scientific facts.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write a paragraph on the birth and lifecycle of stars using figure 20.1
questions.answer: Stars are born out of nebulae, which are clouds of hydrogen gas and dust. Due to gravity, the cloud contracts and becomes dense and hot, forming a star. Depending on their initial mass, stars evolve into red giants or super red giants, and finally end their life as white dwarfs, neutron stars, or black holes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Visit a planetarium, collect information and present it in your school on Science day.
questions.answer: Students should visit a local planetarium, observe the shows regarding constellations and zodiac signs, take notes on the equipment used, and prepare a chart or presentation for the school event.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: योग्य पाहा जोडीदार !
pairs: फुले व पाने कीटकांना आकर्षित करतात

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: पेंग्विनची त्वचा जाड, पांढऱ्या रंगाची व त्वचेखाली चरबीचे आवरण कशासाठी असते?
questions.answer: बर्फाळ प्रदेशातील अतिशय थंडीपासून संरक्षण करण्यासाठी आणि शरीरातील उष्णता टिकवून ठेवण्यासाठी पेंग्विनची त्वचा जाड असून तिच्याखाली चरबीचे जाड आवरण असते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: पेंग्विन नेहमी थव्याने एकमेकांना चिकटून का राहतात?
questions.answer: थव्याने एकमेकांना चिकटून राहिल्यामुळे शरीराची ऊब टिकून राहते आणि तीव्र थंडी व वाऱ्यापासून संरक्षण मिळते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: ध्रुवीय प्रदेशात कायमस्वरूपी वास्तव्य करण्यासाठी तुम्हांमध्ये कोणते अनुकूलन हवे आणि का?
questions.answer: ध्रुवीय प्रदेशात राहण्यासाठी शरीरावर दाट व लांब केस, जाड त्वचा, त्वचेखाली चरबीचा थर आणि परिसराशी मिळताजुळता पांढरा रंग हवा, जेणेकरून थंडीपासून संरक्षण होईल व भक्षकांपासून बचाव होईल.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: पेंग्विन कोणत्या भौगोलिक प्रदेशात राहतो? का?
questions.answer: पेंग्विन अंटार्क्टिका सारख्या दक्षिण ध्रुवीय बर्फाळ प्रदेशात राहतो, कारण त्याचे शरीर तेथील अतिथंड हवामानासाठी अनुकूलित झालेले असते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खोटे कोण बोलतोय ते ओळखून स्पष्टीकरण द्या.
questions.text: घुबड : माझा डोळा पाच आहे.
questions.answer: घुबड खोटे बोलत आहे. घुबडाला दोनच डोळे असतात आणि ते मानवाप्रमाणे चेहऱ्याच्या समोरच्या बाजूला असतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खोटे कोण बोलतोय ते ओळखून स्पष्टीकरण द्या.
questions.text: कोंबडी : माझी बोटे त्वचेने जोडलेली आहेत.
questions.answer: कोंबडी खोटे बोलत आहे. बदक किंवा राजहंस यांसारख्या जलचर पक्ष्यांची बोटे पोहण्यासाठी त्वचेने जोडलेली असतात, कोंबडीची नाही.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खोटे कोण बोलतोय ते ओळखून स्पष्टीकरण द्या.
questions.text: निवडुंग : माझा मांसल हिरवा भाग हे पान आहे.
questions.answer: निवडुंग खोटे बोलत आहे. निवडुंगाचा मांसल हिरवा भाग हे त्याचे खोड आहे. पाने काट्यांत रूपांतरित झालेली असतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील विधानावर आधारित अनुकूलन संबंधित परिच्छेद लेखन करा.
questions.text: वाळवंटात खूप उष्णता आहे.
questions.answer: वाळवंटातील उष्णतेमुळे तेथील प्राण्यांची त्वचा जाड असते, पाय लांब व तळवे गादीसारखे असतात. पाणी टिकवून ठेवण्यासाठी वनस्पतींची पाने काट्यांत रूपांतरित होतात व खोड मांसल बनते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील विधानावर आधारित अनुकूलन संबंधित परिच्छेद लेखन करा.
questions.text: गवताळ प्रदेश हिरवागार असतो.
questions.answer: गवताळ प्रदेशात दाट झुडपे व गवत असते. येथे भक्षक प्राण्यांना लपण्यासाठी हिरवा रंग व वेगाने धावण्यासाठी मजबूत पाय असतात, तर भक्ष्य प्राण्यांचे कान लांब असतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील विधानावर आधारित अनुकूलन संबंधित परिच्छेद लेखन करा.
questions.text: कीटक जास्त प्रमाणात आढळतात.
questions.answer: कीटकांचे शरीर हलके व निमुळते असते. त्यांना उडण्यासाठी पंख व चालण्यासाठी सहा पाय असतात. त्यांच्या या विविध अनुकूलनांमुळे ते सर्वत्र मोठ्या प्रमाणात आढळतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील विधानावर आधारित अनुकूलन संबंधित परिच्छेद लेखन करा.
questions.text: आम्ही लपून बसतो.
questions.answer: अनेक प्राणी शत्रूपासून वाचण्यासाठी किंवा भक्ष्य पकडण्यासाठी परिसराशी मिळताजुळता रंग धारण करतात (छद्मावरण). उदा. सरडा, टोळ किंवा गवताळ प्रदेशातील वाघ.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील विधानावर आधारित अनुकूलन संबंधित परिच्छेद लेखन करा.
questions.text: आमचे कान लांब असतात.
questions.answer: शाकाहारी प्राण्यांचे (उदा. ससा) कान लांब व हलणारे असतात, ज्यामुळे त्यांना दूरचा आवाज ऐकू येतो व धोक्याची पूर्वसूचना मिळून ते स्वतःचे रक्षण करू शकतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: उंटाला 'वाळवंटातील जहाज' का म्हणतात?
questions.answer: उंटाचे पाय लांब व तळवे गादीसारखे असतात, ज्यामुळे तो वाळूत सहज चालतो. तो पाण्याशिवाय अनेक दिवस राहू शकतो आणि त्याच्या नाकावर त्वचेची घडी असते. या अनुकूलनांमुळे तो वाळवंटातील प्रवासासाठी एकमेव साधन ठरतो.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: निवडुंग, बाभूळ व इतर वाळवंटी वनस्पती कमी पाण्याच्या प्रदेशात सहज का जगू शकतात?
questions.answer: या वनस्पतींची पाने काट्यांत रूपांतरित झाल्यामुळे बाष्पोत्सर्जन कमी होते. त्यांची खोडे पाणी व अन्न साठवून मांसल बनतात आणि मुळे पाण्याचा शोध घेण्यासाठी जमिनीत खोलवर जातात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: सजीवांमधील अनुकूलन आणि त्यांच्या सभोवतालची परिस्थिती यांच्यात काय संबंध आहे?
questions.answer: सजीव ज्या परिसरात राहतात, तेथील हवामान, अन्न आणि शत्रू यांच्याशी जुळवून घेण्यासाठी त्यांच्या शरीराच्या अवयवांत व जीवनपद्धतीत कालानुरूप बदल होतात, यालाच अनुकूलन म्हणतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.text: सजीवांचे वर्गीकरण कसे केले जाते?
questions.answer: सजीवांचे वर्गीकरण त्यांच्यातील गुणधर्मांमधील साम्य व फरक यांवर आधारित उतरंडीनुसार केले जाते. यात सृष्टी, संघ, वर्ग, कुल, प्रजाती व जाती अशा टप्प्यांचा वापर होतो. कार्ल लिनिअसची द्विनाम पद्धती यासाठी वापरली जाते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: आदिमानवापासून आजच्या मानवापर्यंत झालेले अनुकूलन कसे घडत गेले असेल, याची माहिती मिळवा.
questions.answer: मानवाचा ताठ कणा, मेंदूचा वाढलेला आकार, हाताच्या अंगठ्याची पकड आणि भाषेचा विकास हे महत्त्वाचे अनुकूलन बदल आहेत.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: काही आवरणी फळे असणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: वाटाणा, घेवडा, शेंगदाणा

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: खोडावर काटे असणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: गुलाब, निवडुंग, बाभळ

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: लाल फुले असणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: जास्वंद, गुलाब, पळस

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: पिवळी फुले असणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: सूर्यफूल, चाफा, झेंडू

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: रात्री पाने मिटणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: गुलमोहर, आवळा, लाजाळू

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: एकच बी असणारी फळे असणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: आंबा, बोर, काजू

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खालील वैशिष्ट्ये असणाऱ्या वनस्पतींची नावे लिहा.
questions.text: फळामध्ये अनेक बिया असणाऱ्या वनस्पती
questions.answer: कलिंगड, पेरू, पपई

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: त्याचे विविध भाग आकृतीसह स्पष्ट करून त्यांचे वर्णन तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.answer: फुलाचे मुख्य भाग निदलपुंज, दलपुंज, पुमंग आणि जायांग हे आहेत. निदलपुंज कळी अवस्थेत संरक्षण करते. दलपुंज पाकळ्यांनी बनलेला असतो. पुमंग हा नर भाग असून तो परागकण तयार करतो, तर जायांग हा मादी भाग असून त्यात अंडाशय असते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: ज्वारी आणि मूग
questions.answer: ज्वारी हे एकदल धान्य असून तिचे मूळ तंतुमय असते. मूग हे द्विदल कडधान्य असून त्याचे मूळ सोटमूळ असते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: कांदा आणि कोथिंबीर
questions.answer: कांदा ही एकदल वनस्पती असून तिची मुळे तंतुमय असतात. कोथिंबीर ही द्विदल वनस्पती असून तिचे मूळ सोटमूळ असते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: केळीचे पान व आंब्याचे पान
questions.answer: केळीच्या पानात समांतर शिराविन्यास असतो, तर आंब्याच्या पानात जाळीदार शिराविन्यास असतो.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: नारळाचे झाड व ज्वारीचे ताट
questions.answer: नारळाचे झाड हे उंच वाढणारे बहुवार्षिक झाड आहे, तर ज्वारीचे ताट हे कमी उंचीचे हंगामी पीक आहे. दोन्हीमध्ये तंतुमय मुळे असतात.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: बीजांकुरण प्रक्रियेचे (आदिमूळ व अंकुर) स्पष्टीकरण तुमच्या शब्दांत लिहा.
questions.answer: बीज रुजताना जमिनीच्या दिशेने वाढणाऱ्या भागाला आदिमूळ म्हणतात, ज्यापासून पुढे मूळ तयार होते. जमिनीच्या वर वाढणाऱ्या भागाला अंकुर म्हणतात, ज्यापासून पुढे खोड विकसित होते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: वनस्पतींच्या विविध अवयवांची (मूळ, खोड, पान, फूल) कार्ये स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: मूळ वनस्पतीला आधार देते व पाणी शोषते. खोड पानांना आधार देते व अन्न-पाण्याचे वहन करते. पाने प्रकाशसंश्लेषणाद्वारे अन्न तयार करतात. फूल पुनरुत्पादनाचे कार्य करते व फळात रूपांतरित होते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: खाली पानांचे काही गुणधर्म दिलेले आहेत. प्रत्येक गुणधर्माचे एक पान शोधून वनस्पतीचे वर्णन लिहा.
questions.text: गुळगुळीत पृष्ठभाग, खडबडीत पृष्ठभाग, लोमश पर्णपत्र, पर्णकोष, काटे.
questions.answer: केळीचे पान गुळगुळीत असते. पारिजातकाचे पान खडबडीत असते. लाजाळूचे पान लोमश असते. मक्याच्या पानात पर्णकोष असतो, तर निवडुंगाच्या पानांचे रूपांतर काट्यांत झालेले असते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: दिलेल्या आकृतीतील (शब्दकोडे) अक्षरे वापरून वनस्पतींच्या भागांची नावे शोधा.
questions.text: दिलेल्या आकृतीत तुम्ही अभ्यासलेल्या वनस्पतींच्या विविध भागांची नावे शोधून लिहा.
questions.answer: सोटमूळ, खोड, पान, फूल, फळ, बी, अंडाशय, परागकण, पाकळी, देठ.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: रिकाम्या जागी कंसातील योग्य शब्द लिहा. (तापमान, आकारमान, वस्तुमान, घनता, आर्द्रता, आर्त्तभूमी, वजन, उदासीन, आकार)
questions.text: अ. हवेची बाष्प धरून ठेवण्याची क्षमता हवेच्या ______ प्रमाणे ठरते.
questions.answer: तापमान

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: रिकाम्या जागी कंसातील योग्य शब्द लिहा. (तापमान, आकारमान, वस्तुमान, घनता, आर्द्रता, आर्त्तभूमी, वजन, उदासीन, आकार)
questions.answer: आकार, वस्तुमान, आकारमान

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: रिकाम्या जागी कंसातील योग्य शब्द लिहा. (तापमान, आकारमान, वस्तुमान, घनता, आर्द्रता, आर्त्तभूमी, वजन, उदासीन, आकार)
questions.text: इ. पाणी गोठवल्यानचे ______ वाढते.
questions.answer: आकारमान

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: रिकाम्या जागी कंसातील योग्य शब्द लिहा. (तापमान, आकारमान, वस्तुमान, घनता, आर्द्रता, आर्त्तभूमी, वजन, उदासीन, आकार)
questions.text: ई. ______ मृदेचा pH 7 असतो.
questions.answer: उदासीन

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: अ. हवा हे वेगवेगळ्या वायूंचे एकजिनसी मिश्रण आहे.
questions.answer: हवेमध्ये नायट्रोजन, ऑक्सिजन, कार्बन डायऑक्साइड यांसारखे अनेक वायू आणि धुलिकण असतात. हे सर्व घटक एकमेकांत अशा प्रकारे मिसळलेले असतात की ते वेगळे ओळखता येत नाहीत, म्हणून हवा हे एकजिनसी मिश्रण आहे.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: आ. पाण्याला वैश्विक द्रावक म्हटले जाते.
questions.answer: पाण्यामध्ये अनेक प्रकारचे पदार्थ (स्थायू, द्रव, वायू) सहजपणे विरघळतात, म्हणून पाण्याला वैश्विक द्रावक म्हटले जाते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: इ. स्वयंपोषीसाठी पाण्याचेशिवाय दुसरा पर्याय नाही.
questions.answer: स्वयंपोषी वनस्पतींना अन्न तयार करण्यासाठी (प्रकाशसंश्लेषण) पाण्याची आवश्यकता असते. तसेच वनस्पतींच्या शरीरातील सर्व जैविक प्रक्रिया पाण्याचे माध्यमातूनच पार पडतात, म्हणून पाण्याशिवाय दुसरा पर्याय नाही.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: अ. हवेतील बाष्पाचे प्रमाण वाढले.
questions.answer: हवेतील बाष्पाचे प्रमाण वाढल्यास हवेतील आर्द्रता वाढते आणि हवा दमट होते. यामुळे आपल्याला घाम जास्त येतो आणि कपडे लवकर वाळत नाहीत.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: आ. जमिनीत सातत्याने एकच पीक घेतले.
questions.answer: जमिनीत सातत्याने एकच पीक घेतल्यास जमिनीतील विशिष्ट पोषक द्रव्यांचा साठा संपतो, जमिनीचा कस कमी होतो आणि उत्पादकता घटते.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: खालील 'अ' गट व 'ब' गट यांच्या योग्य जोड्या लावा.
