questions.answer: True. Tomato wilt is caused by a plant virus that affects the vascular system of the plant.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: State the merits of Whittaker's method of classification.
questions.answer: Whittaker's method is based on cell structure, complexity of organisms, and mode of nutrition. It clearly separates prokaryotes from eukaryotes and distinguishes fungi from plants based on their saprophytic nutrition.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: Write the characteristics of viruses.
questions.answer: Viruses are extremely small (10-100 nm), considered at the edge of living and non-living. They consist of DNA or RNA with a protein coat and can only reproduce inside living host cells.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: Explain the nutrition in fungi.
questions.answer: Fungi are saprophytic organisms. They absorb their nourishment from decaying organic matter by releasing enzymes to break down complex materials.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: Which living organisms are included in the kingdom monera?
questions.answer: Kingdom Monera includes all unicellular, prokaryotic organisms, such as various types of bacteria and blue-green algae.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: I don't have true nucleus, cell organelles or plasma membrane.
questions.answer: Virus (or Bacterium/Prokaryote)

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: I have nucleus and membrane bound cell organelles.
questions.answer: Eukaryote

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: I live on decaying organic matter.
questions.answer: Fungi

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: I reproduce mainly by cell division.
questions.answer: Bacteria

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: I can produce my replica.
questions.answer: Virus

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: I am green, but don't have organs.
questions.answer: Algae

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: Different types of bacteria.
questions.answer: Student should draw Coccus, Coccobacillus, Bacillus, Vibrio (comma shaped), and Spirillum.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: Paramoecium
questions.answer: Student should draw a slipper-shaped organism with cilia, cytostome, and nuclei.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.text: Bacteriophage.
questions.answer: Student should draw the head (containing DNA), collar, sheath, and tail fibers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Living World and Classification of Microbes
questions.instruction: Arrange the following in ascending order of size.
questions.text: Bacteria, Fungi, Viruses, Algae.
questions.answer: Viruses (10 nm to 100 nm) < Bacteria (1 μm to 10 μm) < Fungi (10 μm to 100 μm) < Algae (10 μm to 100 μm).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Infectious and non-infectious diseases.
questions.answer: Infectious diseases spread from an infected person to a healthy person through contaminated air, water, food, or vectors (e.g., Tuberculosis, Dengue). Non-infectious diseases do not spread through contact or media and are caused by internal factors like heredity or lifestyle (e.g., Diabetes, Cancer).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Malaria, hepatitis, elephantiasis, dengue.
questions.answer: Hepatitis (It is spread through contaminated water/needles/blood, while others are spread through insect bites).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plague, AIDS, cholera, T.B.
questions.answer: AIDS (It is a viral disease, while the others are bacterial diseases).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer in one to two sentences.
questions.text: Which are various media of spreading the infectious diseases?
questions.answer: Infectious diseases spread through contaminated air, water, food, insects, and other animals (vectors), as well as through direct physical contact.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer in one to two sentences.
questions.text: Give the names of five non-infectious diseases other than given in the lesson.
questions.answer: Five non-infectious diseases are: 1. Cataract, 2. Arthritis, 3. Kidney stones, 4. Osteoporosis, and 5. Migraine.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer in one to two sentences.
questions.text: Which are the main reasons of diabetes and heart diseases?
questions.answer: The main reasons include heredity, obesity, lack of physical exercise, mental stress, improper diet (junk food), and addictions like smoking or alcoholism.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What can be achieved/can be prevented by the following action?
questions.text: Drinking boiled and filtered water.
questions.answer: It prevents water-borne infectious diseases like cholera, typhoid, dysentery, and hepatitis by killing pathogens present in the water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What can be achieved/can be prevented by the following action?
questions.text: Avoiding smoking and alcoholism.
questions.answer: It prevents various types of cancers (especially mouth and lung cancer), liver cirrhosis, and disorders of the nervous and digestive systems.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What can be achieved/can be prevented by the following action?
questions.text: Regular balanced diet and exercise.
questions.answer: It helps maintain a healthy body weight, boosts immunity, and prevents lifestyle diseases like obesity, diabetes, and heart diseases.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: What can be achieved/can be prevented by the following action?
questions.text: Proper checking of blood before blood donation.
questions.answer: It prevents the transmission of blood-borne infectious diseases like AIDS and Hepatitis B from the donor to the recipient.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Read the passage and answer the question: Master ‘X’ is a 3 year old child. He is living with his family in a slum. Public toilet is present near his house. His father is drunkard. His mother does not know the importance of balanced diet.
questions.text: Master ‘X’ can suffer from which different possible diseases in above conditions?
questions.answer: He can suffer from infectious diseases like cholera or typhoid due to poor sanitation, and deficiency diseases or malnutrition due to lack of a balanced diet.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Read the passage and answer the question: Master ‘X’ is a 3 year old child. He is living with his family in a slum. Public toilet is present near his house. His father is drunkard. His mother does not know the importance of balanced diet.
questions.text: How will you help him and his family in this situation?
questions.answer: I will educate the mother about nutritious food, explain the importance of cleanliness and handwashing, and encourage the father to join a de-addiction center.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Read the passage and answer the question: Master ‘X’ is a 3 year old child. He is living with his family in a slum. Public toilet is present near his house. His father is drunkard. His mother does not know the importance of balanced diet.
questions.text: Which disease can occur to the father of master ‘X’?
questions.answer: The father may suffer from liver cirrhosis, digestive system disorders, or cancers of the mouth, esophagus, or liver due to chronic alcoholism.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give the preventive measures of the following disease.
questions.text: Dengue.
questions.answer: Prevent water stagnation in coolers/pots to stop mosquito breeding, use mosquito nets/repellents, and ensure the surroundings are clean.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give the preventive measures of the following disease.
questions.text: Cancer.
questions.answer: Avoid tobacco, smoking, and alcohol; consume a balanced diet with plenty of leafy vegetables and fruits; and maintain regular physical exercise.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give the preventive measures of the following disease.
questions.text: AIDS.
questions.answer: Ensure safe blood transfusions by testing blood, use only disposable or sterilized needles/syringes, and maintain safe sexual practices.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Explain the importance of the following.
questions.text: Balanced diet.
questions.answer: A balanced diet provides all necessary nutrients in correct proportions, which increases immunity, prevents deficiency diseases, and ensures proper physical and mental growth.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Explain the importance of the following.
questions.text: Physical exercise / Yogasanas.
questions.answer: Exercise and Yogasanas improve blood circulation, reduce mental stress, prevent obesity and heart diseases, and keep the body flexible and energetic.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Make a list of the following.
questions.text: Viral diseases.
questions.answer: Common cold, Influenza, AIDS, Hepatitis, Dengue, Measles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Make a list of the following.
questions.text: Bacterial diseases.
questions.answer: Tuberculosis, Cholera, Typhoid, Plague, Leprosy.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Make a list of the following.
questions.text: Diseases spread through insects.
questions.answer: Malaria, Dengue, Elephantiasis, Plague.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Make a list of the following.
questions.text: Hereditary diseases.
questions.answer: Diabetes (can be hereditary), Sickle cell anemia, Hemophilia, Down syndrome.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write the information on modern diagnostics and treatments of cancer.
questions.answer: Modern diagnostics include CT scans, MRI scans, Mammography, and Biopsy. Treatments involve conventional methods like Chemotherapy, Radiation therapy, and Surgery, along with modern techniques like Robotic and Laparoscopic surgery.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Enlist the names and composition of the medicines present at your home.
questions.answer: Student should list medicines like Paracetamol (for fever), Cetirizine (for allergies), or Antacids, noting their active ingredients from the packaging.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with appropriate words.
questions.text: The SI unit of pressure is N/m², which is also known as _______.
questions.answer: Pascal (Pa)

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: State whether the following statement is True or False.
questions.text: Pressure is a vector quantity.
questions.answer: False

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the types of force and units with their correct descriptions:
pairs: Tendency to remain in existing state
questions.answer: Muscular Force - Contact force; Electrostatic Force - Non-contact force; 1 bar - 10^5 Pa; Inertia - Tendency to remain in existing state

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the common name given to all gases and liquids that exert pressure on the walls of their container?
questions.answer: Fluid

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the figure and answer the question.
questions.text: In the given figure, various actions are shown. Identify whether these are examples of contact or non-contact forces and justify your answer.
questions.answer: These are contact forces. In these actions, the force is seen to act through a direct contact of the objects (like kicking the ball) or via one more object (like the rope used to pull the dog).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the diagram and explain the observation.
questions.text: In the given figure, what happens to the balloon when water is poured into the bottle, and what does this prove about liquid pressure?
questions.answer: The balloon inflates when water is poured. This proves that the pressure of a liquid acts on the sides of the container as well.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following question in brief.
questions.text: Name the three types of inertia.
questions.answer: 1. Inertia of the state of rest, 2. Inertia of motion, 3. Directional inertia.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Camel’s feet do not penetrate into the sand while walking.
questions.answer: Camel's feet have broad bottom surfaces. Because the area is large, the weight (force) of the camel is exerted over a larger area, which reduces the pressure on the sand. Hence, the feet do not sink.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A force of 1000 N is applied perpendicularly on a wooden plank of area 2 m². Calculate the pressure exerted on the plank.
questions.answer: Pressure = Force / Area = 1000 N / 2 m² = 500 N/m² (or 500 Pa).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why do we not get crushed under the heavy atmospheric pressure acting on our bodies?
questions.answer: We do not get crushed because the cavities in our body are filled with air, and our arteries and veins are filled with blood. This internal pressure balances the external atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Define Pressure.
questions.answer: The force exerted perpendicularly on a unit area is called pressure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If the area on which a constant force is applied increases, the pressure _______.
questions.answer: decreases

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the net force acting on an object if two equal forces are applied to it in opposite directions?
questions.answer: The net force (effective force) is zero because the forces are balanced.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A revolving electric fan continues to revolve for some time even after it is switched off. Which type of inertia is this?
questions.answer: Inertia of motion

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Fill in the blanks with appropriate words.
questions.text: The SI unit of potential difference is ______.
questions.answer: Volt (V)

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: State whether the following statement is True or False.
questions.text: Electric current is a scalar quantity.
questions.answer: True

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the electric cells with their characteristics or uses:
questions.answer: Lead-Acid cell - 2V potential difference; Ni-Cd cell - 1.2V and rechargeable; Lithium-ion cell - Used in Laptops; Dry cell - Uses Zinc metal layer

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which scientist first observed that a magnetic field is created when an electric current flows in a wire?
questions.answer: Hans Christian Oerstead

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If four dry cells, each having a potential difference of 1.5 V, are connected in a series to form a battery, what will be the total potential difference of the battery?
questions.answer: Total potential difference = 1.5 V + 1.5 V + 1.5 V + 1.5 V = 6.0 V

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the given figure and answer the question.
questions.text: In the given figure of an electrical circuit, why is the bulb not glowing?
questions.answer: The bulb is not glowing because there is no potential difference in the circuit due to the absence of an electric cell.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the given figure and answer the question.
questions.text: In the given figure of a dry cell, identify the material used for the central rod which acts as the positive terminal.
questions.answer: The central rod is a graphite rod.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Dry cells are more convenient to use than cells containing liquids.
questions.answer: Dry cells can be held in any direction with respect to the ground and can be used in mobile instruments because they do not contain free-flowing liquids that could spill.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is an electrolyte and what is its function in a cell?
questions.answer: An electrolyte is a wet pulp or liquid containing negatively and positively charged ions. These ions are the carriers of electricity and allow current to flow through chemical reactions.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Electrostatic Potential
questions.answer: The electric level deciding the direction of flow of electric charges is called electrostatic potential.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If 10 Coulombs of electrical charge flows through a wire in 5 seconds, calculate the electric current in Amperes.
questions.answer: Electric current (I) = Charge / Time = 10 C / 5 s = 2 A (Ampere).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain the construction and working of an electromagnet based on the activity described in the text.
questions.answer: An electromagnet is made by winding a copper wire around an iron screw. When current flows through the wire, magnetism is produced in the coil, making the screw act as a magnet. As soon as the current stops, the magnetism vanishes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In which direction does conventional current flow in a circuit?
questions.answer: Conventional current flows from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a cell.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the difference in the atomic models of Thomson and Rutherford?
questions.answer: Thomson's model proposed a uniform distribution of positive charge with embedded electrons (like plum pudding), while Rutherford's model proposed a central, dense, positively charged nucleus with electrons revolving around it in the surrounding empty space.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is meant by valency of an element? What is the relationship between the number of valence electron and valency?
questions.answer: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom. The number of valence electrons determines valency: if valence electrons are 1-4, valency equals that number; if 5-8, valency is usually (8 - number of valence electrons).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is meant by atomic mass number? Explain how the atomic number and mass number of carbon are 6 and 12 respectively.
questions.answer: Atomic mass number is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Carbon has 6 protons (atomic number = 6) and 6 neutrons, therefore its mass number is 6 + 6 = 12.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is meant by subatomic particle? Give brief information of three subatomic particles with reference to electrical charge.
questions.answer: Subatomic particles are the constituent particles within an atom. The three main ones are: Protons (positively charged, +1e), Electrons (negatively charged, -1e), and Neutrons (electrically neutral, 0 charge).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: The intermolecular force is ______ in the particles of solid.
questions.answer: maximum

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: Solids retain their volume even when external pressure is applied. This property is called ______.
questions.answer: incompressibility

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: Matter is classified into the types mixture, compound and element, by applying the criterion ______.
questions.answer: chemical composition of matter

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: Matter that contain two or more constituent substances is called ______.
questions.answer: mixture

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: Milk is an example of type of matter called ______.
questions.answer: heterogeneous mixture

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: Water, mercury and bromine are similar to each other, because three are ______.
questions.answer: liquids

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Choose the appropriate option and rewrite the following statement.
questions.text: Valency of carbon is 4 and that of oxygen is 2. From this, we understand that there are ______ chemical bond/bonds between the carbon atom and one oxygen atom in the compound-carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Identify the odd term out and explain.
questions.text: Gold, silver, copper, brass
questions.answer: Brass. Gold, silver, and copper are elements, while brass is an alloy (mixture).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Identify the odd term out and explain.
questions.text: Hydrogen, hydrogen peroxide, carbon dioxide, water vapour.
questions.answer: Hydrogen. Hydrogen is an element, while the others are compounds.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Identify the odd term out and explain.
questions.text: Milk, lemon juice, carbon, steel.
questions.answer: Carbon. Carbon is an element, while others are mixtures.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Identify the odd term out and explain.
questions.text: Water, mercury, bromine, petrol.
questions.answer: Petrol. Petrol is a mixture, while others are pure substances (elements or compounds).

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Identify the odd term out and explain.
questions.text: Sugar, salt, baking soda, blue vitriol.
questions.answer: Sugar. Sugar is an organic compound, while others are inorganic compounds.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Identify the odd term out and explain.
questions.text: Hydrogen, sodium, potassium, carbon.
questions.answer: Carbon. Carbon is a non-metal with valency 4, while others have valency 1.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plants synthesize glucose in sunlight with the help of chlorophyll from carbon dioxide and water and give away oxygen. Identify the four compounds in this process and name their types.
questions.answer: The four compounds are: 1. Glucose (Organic compound), 2. Chlorophyll (Complex compound), 3. Carbon dioxide (Inorganic compound), 4. Water (Inorganic compound).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In one sample of brass, the following ingredients were found : copper (70%) and zinc (30%). Identify the solvent, solute and solution from these.
questions.answer: Solution: Brass; Solvent: Copper (70%); Solute: Zinc (30%).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Sea water tastes salty due to the dissolved salt. The salinity (the proportion of salts in water) of some water bodies Lonar lake - 7.9 %, Pacific Ocean 3.5 %, Mediterranean sea - 3.8 %. Dead sea - 33.7 %. Explain two characteristics of mixtures from the above information.
questions.answer: 1. The constituent substances of a mixture retain their individual properties (e.g., salt remains salty). 2. The proportion of constituent substances in a mixture is not fixed and can vary.

questions.answer: Mercury, Bromine

questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Gaseous element
questions.answer: Hydrogen, Oxygen

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Solid element

questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.

questions.answer: Sugar syrup, Air

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Colloid
questions.answer: Milk, Fog

questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Organic compound
questions.answer: Glucose, Urea

questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Complex compound
questions.answer: Chlorophyll, Haemoglobin

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Inorganic compound
questions.answer: Common salt, Limestone

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Metalloid
questions.answer: Silicon, Arsenic

questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Element with valency 1
questions.answer: Hydrogen, Sodium

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Give two examples of the following.
questions.text: Element with valency 2
questions.answer: Magnesium, Calcium

questions.instruction: Write the names and symbols of the constituent elements and identify their valencies from the molecular formulae given below.
questions.text: KCl, HBr, MgBr2, K2O, NaH, CaCl2, CCl4, HI, H2S, Na2S, FeS, BaCl2

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: In the given figure, a table showing the chemical composition of some matter is provided. Identify the main type of matter (Element, Compound, or Mixture) for each entry based on its chemical composition.
questions.text: Complete the 'Main type of matter' column for the substances listed in the table.
questions.answer: Sea water: Mixture; Distilled water: Compound; Hydrogen gas: Element; LPG: Mixture; Baking soda: Compound; Pure gold: Element; Oxygen gas: Element; Bronze: Mixture; Diamond: Element; Blue vitriol: Compound; Lime stone: Compound; Dilute HCl: Mixture.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Hydrogen is combustible, oxygen helps combustion, but water helps to extinguish fire.
questions.answer: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen. The properties of a compound are different from those of its constituent elements. While hydrogen is combustible and oxygen supports it, their compound water has the property to extinguish fire.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Constituent substances of a colloid cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.
questions.answer: In a colloid, the size of the particles of the dispersed phase is very small (around 10^-5 m), which is smaller than the pores of an ordinary filter paper. Therefore, they pass through the filter paper.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Lemon sherbat has sweet, sour and salty taste and it can be poured in a glass.
questions.answer: Lemon sherbat is a mixture. It retains the properties of its constituents (sugar, lemon, salt). Being a liquid mixture, it has fluidity and can be poured into a container.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A solid matter has the properties of definite shape and volume.
questions.answer: In solids, the intermolecular forces are very strong. The particles are closely packed and occupy fixed positions, resulting in a definite shape and volume.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Deduce the molecular formulae of the compound obtained from the following pairs of elements by the cross multiplication method.
questions.text: C (Valency 4) & Cl (Valency 1)
questions.answer: CCl4

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Deduce the molecular formulae of the compound obtained from the following pairs of elements by the cross multiplication method.
questions.text: N (Valency 3) & H (Valency 1)
questions.answer: NH3

questions.instruction: Deduce the molecular formulae of the compound obtained from the following pairs of elements by the cross multiplication method.
questions.text: C (Valency 4) & O (Valency 2)
questions.answer: CO2

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Deduce the molecular formulae of the compound obtained from the following pairs of elements by the cross multiplication method.
questions.text: Ca (Valency 2) & O (Valency 2)
questions.answer: CaO

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Complete the table: State the use in everyday life for the given property of metal.
questions.text: Property of metal: Ductility
questions.answer: Ductility allows metals to be drawn into thin wires, such as copper wires used in electrical circuits.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Complete the table: State the use in everyday life for the given property of metal.
questions.text: Property of metal: Malleability
questions.answer: Malleability allows metals to be hammered into thin sheets, like aluminum foils used for wrapping food.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Complete the table: State the use in everyday life for the given property of metal.
questions.text: Property of metal: Conduction of heat
questions.answer: Metals conduct heat, making them ideal for manufacturing cooking utensils like pans and pressure cookers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Complete the table: State the use in everyday life for the given property of metal.
questions.text: Property of metal: Conduction of electricity
questions.answer: Metals conduct electricity, so they are used to make electric cables and components for electronic devices.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Complete the table: State the use in everyday life for the given property of metal.
questions.text: Property of metal: Sonority
questions.answer: Sonority allows metals to produce a ringing sound, which is used in making school bells and musical instruments.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Gold, silver, iron, diamond
questions.answer: Diamond (It is a non-metal/allotrope of carbon, while others are metals).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Ductility, brittleness, sonority, malleability
questions.answer: Brittleness (It is a property of non-metals, while others are properties of metals).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Carbon, bromine, sulphur, phosphorus
questions.answer: Bromine (It is a liquid at room temperature, while others are solids).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Brass, bronze, iron, steel
questions.answer: Iron (It is a pure metal, while others are alloys).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The stainless steel vessels in kitchen have copper coating on the bottom.
questions.answer: Copper is a better conductor of heat than stainless steel. The copper coating ensures that the vessel heats up faster and distributes heat more evenly for cooking.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Copper and brass vessels are cleaned with lemon.
questions.answer: Copper and brass react with moisture and CO2 to form a greenish layer of basic copper carbonate. The citric acid in lemon reacts with this layer and dissolves it, making the vessel shine again.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Sodium metal is kept in kerosene.
questions.answer: Sodium is a highly reactive metal that reacts vigorously with oxygen and moisture in the air, catching fire. It does not react with kerosene, so it is kept submerged in it for safety.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is done to prevent corrosion of metals?
questions.answer: To prevent corrosion, layers of oil, grease, varnish, or paint are applied to metal surfaces. Processes like galvanizing, electroplating, and alloying are also used.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are the metals that make the alloys brass and bronze?
questions.answer: Brass is made from Copper and Zinc. Bronze is made from Copper and Tin.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are the adverse effects of corrosion?
questions.answer: Corrosion causes damage to iron railings, bridges, ships, and car bodies. It leads to the weakening of structures and results in significant economic loss due to metal degradation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are uses of Noble metals?
questions.answer: Noble metals like gold and silver are used for making jewelry, in dentistry, and in electronic gadgets. Platinum is used as a catalyst in chemical reactions.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the three test tubes in the experiment to study rusting and answer the following question.
questions.text: Why the nail in the test tube 2 is not rusted?
questions.answer: In test tube 2, the nail is in boiled water covered with a layer of oil. Boiling removes dissolved air, and the oil prevents new air from dissolving, so the nail does not rust due to lack of oxygen.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the three test tubes in the experiment to study rusting and answer the following question.
questions.text: Why is the nail in the test tube 1 is rusted highly?
questions.answer: In test tube 1, the nail is exposed to both air and water. Rusting is an oxidation process that requires both moisture and oxygen to be present simultaneously.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the three test tubes in the experiment to study rusting and answer the following question.
questions.text: Would the nail in the test tube 3 get rusted?
questions.answer: No, the nail in test tube 3 would not rust because it contains calcium chloride, which absorbs all moisture from the air, and rusting cannot occur in dry air.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How is the 'Varkha' or sliver foil used in sweets made? Collect the information about which metals are used to make 'Varkha'.
questions.answer: 'Varkha' is made by hammering thin strips of metal (usually silver or gold) between sheets of leather or special paper for several hours until they become extremely thin foils. Silver and Gold are the metals used.

questions.answer: Air pollution

questions.answer: Water pollution / Food pollution

questions.instruction: Read the passage and identify the sentences expressing types of pollution.
questions.text: Nilesh is a student of std. VIII and lives in urban area. It takes about an hour to go to the school by bus. He faces the heavy traffic of two wheelers, four wheelers, rickshaws, buses while going to school. He is facing the problem of asthma since last few days. Doctors recommended him to stay away from urban area. Since then, his mother sent him to the village of his maternal uncle. Nilesh saw the heaps of garbage at many places in village. Foul smell of human and animal wastes was present at many places. Blackish water with foul smell was flowing in a stream. He developed some abdominal disease within few days.

questions.answer: 1-b, 2-d, 3-a, 4-e, 5-c. These pollutants enter the human body and cause severe damage to the nervous system, respiratory system, and skin.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is pollution?
questions.answer: Contamination of natural environment that will be harmful to ecosystems is called pollution.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are pollutants?
questions.answer: Factors affecting natural functions of ecosystem and causing harmful effects on abiotic and biotic factors are called pollutants.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is acid rain?
questions.answer: Oxides of sulphur and nitrogen are released into the atmosphere through burning of fossil fuels. Those oxides mix with rain water and form acids like sulphuric acid and nitric acid, which fall with rain. This is called acid rain.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is green house effect?
questions.answer: Gases like CO2, methane, and nitrous oxide trap the infrared radiation reflected by the earth, preventing it from escaping into space. This results in the heating of the earth's atmosphere, known as the greenhouse effect.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which are visible pollutants known to you?
questions.answer: Visible pollutants include plastic waste, sand, sewage, solid garbage, and dust particles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which are invisible pollutants?
questions.answer: Invisible pollutants include various gases like Carbon monoxide, Nitrogen oxides, and microscopic bacteria or fungi.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Give two examples of each of water, soil and air pollution from your residential area.
questions.answer: Air: Smoke from vehicles, dust from construction. Water: Disposal of household sewage in rivers, immersion of idols. Soil: Plastic littering, excessive use of chemical fertilizers in nearby gardens.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How does the pollution occur due to vehicles? Give the names of vehicles causing least pollution.
questions.answer: Vehicles burn fossil fuels and release harmful gases like CO, CO2, and nitrogen oxides. Bicycles and electric vehicles (EVs) cause the least pollution.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are natural reasons for water pollution?
questions.answer: Natural reasons include aquatic weeds, decomposing organic matter, siltation due to floods, and growth of algae.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Suggest four preventive measures for air pollution.
questions.answer: 1. Use of tall chimneys in factories. 2. Regular PUC check of vehicles. 3. Planting more trees. 4. Using clean fuels like CNG or LPG.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain relation between green house effect and global warming.
questions.answer: The greenhouse effect traps heat in the atmosphere. As the concentration of greenhouse gases increases due to pollution, more heat is trapped, leading to a steady rise in the Earth's average temperature, which is called global warming.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Construct two slogans each on air, water and soil pollution.
questions.answer: Air: 'Be a part of the solution, not the pollution.' Water: 'Save water, save life.' Soil: 'Stop soil erosion, keep the earth green.'

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Classify the following pollutants into natural and manmade categories.
questions.text: Sewage, dust, pollen grains, chemical fertilizers, vehicular smoke, algae, pesticides, waste of animals and birds.
questions.answer: Natural: Dust, pollen grains, algae, waste of animals and birds. Manmade: Sewage, chemical fertilizers, vehicular smoke, pesticides.

questions.answer: True

questions.answer: Class A Fire - Wood, clothes, coal; Class B Fire - Petrol, oil, varnish; Class C Fire - Acetylene, L.P.G.; Class E Fire - Electrical components

questions.text: What is the mathematical measuring unit used to measure the intensity of an earthquake?
questions.answer: Richter Scale

questions.answer: Epicentre

questions.answer: Cracks to the buildings caused by an earthquake.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is meant by an earthquake?
questions.answer: Sudden vibrations on the earth and the shaking of the earth surface/ground is called an earthquake.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why should we avoid using a lift in a multistoried building during an earthquake?
questions.answer: During an earthquake, there is a possibility of power failure or the lift getting stuck due to structural damage; therefore, it is safer to use the staircase.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Solve the following based on the text.
questions.text: If the National Earthquakes Information Center observes that 14,000 earthquakes occur on earth in a year of 365 days, approximately how many earthquakes are noticed every day? (Round to the nearest whole number)
questions.answer: 14,000 / 365 = approximately 38 earthquakes per day.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Mention any two causes of landslides.
questions.answer: 1. After effects of natural disasters like heavy rains or floods. 2. Unlimited cutting of trees which causes soil erosion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain the 'Cool Out' method of fire extinction.
questions.answer: Water is used to extinguish fire as it is easily available. Spraying water on or around the fire creates a cooling effect that helps to control and put out the fire.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Potassium, Sodium, Paper, Calcium.
questions.answer: Paper (It is a fuel for Class A fire, while others are metals for Class D fire).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What precautions should you take if you are outside your house during an earthquake?
questions.answer: If outside, park your vehicle at a safe place and sit inside it. Do not wait near or below tall buildings, trees, or electric poles to avoid injury from falling objects.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are Earthquake Resistant Buildings?
questions.answer: The constructions which do not get damaged due to earth movements up to a certain limit are called earthquake resistant buildings.

questions.subject: Science

questions.answer: IS 456 - Construction of tall buildings; IS 1893 - Criteria for earthquake resistant design; IS 13920 - Ductile detailing of reinforced concrete

questions.answer: Mitochondria

questions.answer: Vacuole

questions.answer: Endoplasmic Reticulum

questions.answer: Golgi complex

questions.text: Leaves are green because of me.
questions.answer: Chloroplast (Chlorophyll)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: RBCs had mitochondria.
questions.answer: If RBCs had mitochondria, they would consume the oxygen they carry for their own energy needs, making the transport of oxygen to other body tissues inefficient.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: There had been no difference between mitochondria and plastids.
questions.answer: If there were no difference, the specialized functions of energy production and photosynthesis would be confused; animal cells might have photosynthesized or plant cells might have lacked specific energy conversion efficiency.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Genes had been absent on the chromosomes.
questions.answer: If genes were absent, hereditary traits would not be transmitted from parents to offspring, and the cell would not be able to control protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plasma membrane had not been selectively permeable.
questions.answer: The cell would lose control over the movement of substances. Harmful substances could enter freely and useful materials could leave the cell, eventually leading to cell death.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plants lacked anthocyanin.
questions.answer: Plants would not have violet, blue, or purple colors in their flowers or fruits, which could affect their ability to attract pollinators or seed dispersers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Who is odd man among us? Give reason.
questions.text: Nucleolus, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum
questions.answer: Nucleolus. Reason: It is a component located inside the nucleus, while the others are cell organelles located in the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Who is odd man among us? Give reason.
questions.text: DNA, Ribosomes, Chlorophyll
questions.answer: Chlorophyll. Reason: It is a pigment found in plastids, whereas DNA and Ribosomes are fundamental cellular components involved in genetic information and protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Plasma membrane
questions.answer: It acts as a selectively permeable membrane that regulates the entry and exit of substances and protects the internal components of the cell.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Cytoplasm
questions.answer: It provides a medium for cellular chemical reactions to occur and holds all the cell organelles in place.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Lysosome
questions.answer: It acts as a waste disposal system, digesting worn-out organelles and destroying viruses or bacteria that attack the cell.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Vacuole
questions.answer: It maintains the osmotic pressure of the cell, stores metabolic byproducts, and provides turgidity and rigidity to plant cells.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Nucleus
questions.answer: It controls all metabolic activities of the cell and cell division, and it is responsible for the transmission of hereditary characters.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Match the following substances with the colours they provide.
questions.answer: Red tomato - Lycopene; Green leaf - Chlorophyll; Carrot - Carotene; Violet - Anthocyanin

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Observe the given figure and answer the following question.
questions.text: In the given figure, several tools are shown. Identify the primary instrument used to observe cells and state why it is necessary for studying cell organelles.
questions.answer: The primary instrument is the Compound Microscope. It is necessary because cells and their organelles are microscopic and cannot be seen with the naked eye; the microscope magnifies them so they can be studied.

questions.answer: Respiratory System: Nose, Pharynx, Trachea, Lungs - Respiration. Circulatory System: Heart, Blood vessels, Blood - Transport of nutrients and oxygen.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Human blood is red coloured.
questions.answer: Human blood is red because of the presence of hemoglobin, an iron-containing respiratory pigment found in Red Blood Cells (RBCs).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Upward and downward movement of diaphragm occurs consecutively.
questions.answer: This movement changes the air pressure in the thoracic cavity. Downward movement decreases pressure causing inhalation; upward movement increases pressure causing exhalation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Blood donation is considered to be superior of all donations.
questions.answer: Blood cannot be manufactured artificially. A single donation can save multiple lives during emergencies, making it a life-saving gift that has no substitute.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Person with O blood group is considered as universal donor.
questions.answer: Blood group O does not have A or B antigens on the surface of RBCs, so it can be given to a person with any other blood group without causing an immune reaction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Food must have limited amount of salts.
questions.answer: Excessive salt intake increases the sodium level in the blood, which can lead to high blood pressure (hypertension) and increase the risk of heart disease.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Explain the functional correlation of circulatory system with respiratory, digestive and excretory system.
questions.answer: The respiratory system provides oxygen to the blood; the digestive system provides nutrients. The circulatory system transports these to cells and carries waste to the excretory system for removal.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Explain the structure and function of human blood.
questions.answer: Blood consists of plasma (liquid) and blood cells (RBC, WBC, Platelets). It functions to transport gases, nutrients, and waste, protect against infections, and regulate body temperature.

questions.subject: Science
questions.instruction: Answer the following questions in your own words.
questions.text: Explain the importance and need of blood donation.
questions.answer: Blood donation is essential for patients undergoing surgery, accident victims, and those with blood disorders like anemia. It is a safe process that helps maintain blood bank supplies for emergencies.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Arteries and veins.
questions.answer: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart (except pulmonary artery) and have thick walls. Veins carry deoxygenated blood toward the heart and have thinner walls with valves.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: External and internal respiration.
questions.answer: External respiration is the exchange of gases between lungs and blood. Internal respiration is the exchange of gases between blood and tissue cells.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which health parameters of blood donor should be checked?
questions.answer: Parameters include hemoglobin level, blood pressure, body temperature, weight, and checking for infectious diseases like HIV, Hepatitis, or Malaria.

questions.instruction: Read the following paragraph and identify the disease.
questions.text: Today, her child became one and half year old. However, that child does not seem to be healthy and happy. It was continuously crying and gradually becoming weak. It has shortness of breath. Its nails have become blue.
questions.answer: The child is likely suffering from a congenital heart disease (often called 'Blue Baby Syndrome'), which causes poor oxygenation of blood.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Your neighboring uncle has been diagnosed with hypertension. What should he do to keep his blood pressure within normal range?
questions.answer: He should reduce salt intake, exercise regularly, manage stress through yoga or meditation, avoid smoking/alcohol, and take prescribed medicines regularly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Collect information about various modern treatments on heart diseases.
questions.answer: Student should research topics like angioplasty, bypass surgery, heart transplant, and pacemakers.

questions.answer: 1. Acid or Neutral (No change in Phenolphthalein), 2. Acid (Methyl orange turns red), 3. Base (Red litmus turns blue).

questions.subject: Science

questions.answer: H₂SO₄: Sulphuric acid, Ca(OH)₂: Calcium hydroxide, HCl: Hydrochloric acid, NaOH: Sodium hydroxide, KOH: Potassium hydroxide, NH₄OH: Ammonium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Sulphuric acid has highest importance in chemical Industry. Why?
questions.answer: Sulphuric acid is used in the manufacture of fertilizers, explosives, chemicals, dyes, drugs, and in car batteries. Because of its wide range of applications, it is known as the 'King of Chemicals'.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which acid is used for getting chloride salt?
questions.answer: Hydrochloric acid (HCl)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: By squeezing lemon on a piece of rock the gas liberated turned lime water milky, which compound is present in the rock?
questions.answer: The rock contains a carbonate compound (like Calcium Carbonate). When citric acid from lemon reacts with it, Carbon dioxide gas is released, which turns lime water milky.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The label on the bottle of chemical is spoiled. How will you find whether the chemical is acidic or not?
questions.answer: We can test the chemical using an indicator like blue litmus paper. If the blue litmus turns red, the chemical is acidic. Alternatively, we can use pH paper or other indicators like methyl orange.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain the difference between acid and base.
questions.answer: Acids have a sour taste and contain H+ ions as the main constituent. They turn blue litmus red. Bases have a bitter taste, are slippery to touch, and contain OH- ions as the main constituent. They turn red litmus blue.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why indicator does not get affected by salt?
questions.answer: Indicators change color based on the concentration of H+ or OH- ions. Salts are generally neutral products of neutralization and do not possess excess H+ or OH- ions to change the color of indicators.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which substances are produced by neutralization process?
questions.answer: Salt and water are produced by the neutralization process.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which are the industrial uses of acids?
questions.answer: Industrial uses include: 1. Production of fertilizers. 2. Refining of petroleum. 3. Manufacture of explosives, paints, and drugs. 4. Cleaning of metal surfaces (pickling).

questions.answer: A precipitate is a white insoluble solid that settles at the bottom of a solution during a chemical reaction.

questions.answer: Noble gases do not form chemical bonds because their electron octet or duplet is already complete, making them stable.

questions.text: Write the electronic configuration of Sodium (Atomic number 11) and Chlorine (Atomic number 17).
questions.answer: Sodium (Na): 2, 8, 1; Chlorine (Cl): 2, 8, 7

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain the formation of an ionic bond in Sodium Chloride (NaCl).
questions.answer: Sodium atom gives its one valence electron to a chlorine atom, forming a Na+ cation and a Cl- anion. Due to the electrostatic force of attraction between these opposite charges, an ionic bond is formed.

questions.subject: Science

questions.text: In the given figure showing various changes like ripening and rusting, state two perceivable observations that indicate a chemical change has occurred.
questions.answer: Perceivable observations include change in colour (as seen in the fruit) and change in taste or release of gases.

questions.answer: The effervescence indicates the liberation of carbon dioxide gas during the chemical reaction between citric acid and sodium bicarbonate.

questions.answer: CO₂ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why does lime water turn milky when we blow into it with a blow tube?
questions.answer: Lime water turns milky because the carbon dioxide in our breath reacts with calcium hydroxide to form a white insoluble precipitate of calcium carbonate.

questions.answer: Thermometer

questions.text: Define one calorie heat.
questions.answer: One calorie heat is the heat required to increase the temperature of 1 gm of water through 1°C.
